column1: # clues.tsv for ft_substr -- pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# Lines are shown most-fundamental first; the first line doubles as the "foothold".
Which index of s holds the substring's first byte, and what does "a maximum length of ’len’" (p.10) let the substring be shorter than?
When len reaches past the end of s, how many bytes of s are really there to take from start, and how many does your block need for them and its terminator?
len is a size_t: what happens to a sum like start + len, or to len + 1, when len is SIZE_MAX or close to it?
UINT_MAX is the largest value an unsigned int holds. Does a size_t hold more on the machine your code runs on, and is len, or a count made from it, ever kept in a type that holds less than a size_t?
Is a tab, a line break or a byte above 0x7f anything other than one more byte to your function? Where could a char's sign or value change what you copy?
Nothing in the subject bounds s, start or len. Does anything in your function stop working once they pass a few thousand bytes?
